transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes approx
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Rajiv (Redwood SE), Elena (CSM); Liam (CTO), Priya (Head of Data), Marco (SRE), Sofia (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): discuss POC scope, confirm security checklist and benchmark plan; timeline to run benchmarks mid-May, Redwood to send SOC2 docs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick round — can we do quick intros?
[00:10] Liam (Sycamore): Yeah Liam here, CTO, overseeing infra and data.
[00:17] Priya (Sycamore): Priya, head of data, I'll own model OKRs and acceptance tests.
[00:21] Marco (Sycamore): Marco, SRE, I get called in for networking and perf tests.
[00:26] Sofia (Sycamore): Sofia PM, coordinating timelines.
[00:30] Maya: Great. Rajiv and I will run through target success criteria, sizing questions, and then dig into security gates.
[00:40] Rajiv (Redwood): Quick note: we'll want to capture both recommendation and conversational search workloads — they behave pretty differently in token cost and latency.
[00:48] Priya: Yep, we have two flows: 1) inline product recommender (short prompts, high QPS) and 2) conversational search for CS agents (longer context, persistent sessions).
[00:58] Rajiv: Perfect. For sizing, can you give ballpark concurrency and qps?
[01:05] Priya: Peak concurrency around 250 concurrent agents for recommender, steady QPS ~200, bursts to 800 QPS for promos. For convo search maybe 50 concurrent sessions, average 1.5k tokens per session.
[01:20] Rajiv: Good, that's helpful. For the pilot we usually run scaled-down but realistic workloads — do you have a sample traffic trace or a replay?
[01:28] Liam: We can share production-sanitized traces, yes. We'll strip PII before sending.
[01:33] Maya: Awesome. Moving to success criteria — Priya, what would make this a clear pass?
[01:41] Priya: Three things: latency SLOs met (p95 sub-300ms for recommender), correctness/quality measured by our relevance precision@10 baseline, and security/compliance gates: SOC2 readiness and SSO integration with our IdP. Also audit logs for every inference call retained for 90 days.
[02:01] Rajiv: Sub-300ms p95 is tight but doable on dedicated instances with batching tuned. We should define the exact prompt sizes for that metric. For convo search p95 we'll likely be higher — acceptable threshold?
[02:12] Priya: For convo search p95 under 1.2s would be acceptable.
[02:16] Rajiv: Noted.
[02:18] Maya: On audits, Redwood can stream structured audit logs and provide an ELK/Cloudwatch-compatible format — Rajiv can confirm fields.
[02:26] Rajiv: We'll emit request id, model version, user token (masked), latency, decision route (hosted/dedicated), and KMS envelope key id if encryption used. There might be a couple small mismatches in field names vs your schema, but we can map.
[02:40] Marco: Important for us is the tamper-evidence and retention — can logs be WORM or forward to our S3 bucket with object lock?
[02:48] Rajiv: We can forward logs to your cloud storage and retain them; object lock/OCR is on your side, but we can support signed logs and signing via KMS to show provenance.
[03:00] Maya: Let's step back to deployment options for the pilot — hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC. Marco, Liam, any constraints?
[03:09] Marco: Security team prefers private control plane with VPC peering for the POC, because we've got internal data classified as confidential.
[03:17] Liam: Agree — for the pilot we want private VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. If pilot is successful we'll talk Dedicated reserved capacity.
[03:26] Rajiv: For a private deployment we need a handful of infra pieces — minimal is a pair of GPU nodes, NAT/egress rules and a peering connection. We can run the pilot in your cloud account or in a redwood-managed private tenant with VPC peering, whichever you prefer.
[03:40] Marco: Prefer in our account; we have strict egress rules.
[03:44] Rajiv: Understood. We'll send the infra checklist.
[03:48] Sofia: Timeline — we're targeting internal stakeholder demo on June 2nd. What scheduling would the Redwood pilot need?
[03:55] Maya: To hit early June demo, we'd propose a 2-week pilot starting around May 18th: week 1 benchmarking/setup, week 2 validation and acceptance. That aligns with the benchmark window you all wanted.
[04:07] Priya: That sounds fine.
[04:09] Rajiv: We'll need access to sanitized traces, sample prompts and an SSO test account for the IdP.
[04:15] Priya: We'll provision those.
[04:18] Maya: OK security deep dive — SOC 2/ISO. We can provide our SOC 2 Type II summary report and ISO 27001 mapping sheet. Anything specific you need from the report?
[04:29] Liam: We'd like the scope details — whether hosting and inference runtime are included in the scope, and third-party subprocessor list. Also duration of last audit.
[04:38] Maya: We'll include scope and last audit period in the package. Redwood's hosted runtime is in scope for our SOC2; private deployments are covered differently — we'll include guidance.
[04:47] Marco: A couple more: SAML metadata, SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated flows, SCIM support for user provisioning?
[04:56] Rajiv: We support SAML 2.0, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated. SCIM for group sync is available for enterprise plans; for pilot we can demo SAML and manual group mapping.
[05:07] Priya: RBAC — we need role separation so devs can't see audit logs and only security can access them. Can you support fine-grained roles?
[05:15] Rajiv: Yes, RBAC is built-in. Roles can be mapped to SAML assertions via groups. We'll show a role matrix in the SOW.
[05:23] Marco: KMS — we want customer-managed keys (BYOK) for encrypting cached KV and logs. Is HSM support available?
[05:31] Rajiv: We support CMK integrations with major cloud KMS providers; HSM-backed keys are supported where the cloud provider exposes them. For on-prem HSMs we have a connector option but it's more involved.
[05:43] Maya: Noted — we'll include KMS integration docs.
[05:46] Sofia: Audit log format — Priya wants structured events, what fields are included again?
[05:53] Rajiv: See earlier: request_id, timestamp, model_version, route, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, user_id (hashed), decision (served_by), and enrichments like reason code for fallback. We can add custom fields.
[06:08] Priya: Hashing user_id is important. Also need to ensure logs are immutable once written.
[06:14] Rajiv: We'll sign events with envelope signatures and you can ingest into your WORM-enabled bucket.
[06:20] Liam: Can we do an attestation that logs weren't altered?
[06:24] Rajiv: Yes, we can provide signed digests and a timestamping service for the pilot.
[06:31] Maya: Benchmarks — Rajiv, can you propose measurement targets for recommender and convo search?
[06:36] Rajiv: For recommender: aim for 200 QPS sustained with p95 < 300ms for the prompt sizes you provided; target tokens/sec metric and cost per 1k requests. For convo search: run with session affinity and KV caching enabled — measure cold vs warm p95 (cold might be ~800-1kms, warm under 1.2s). We'll capture throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, and token/sec.
[06:59] Marco: How do we measure cost? We want per-request cost and per-concurrent-user cost using your unit economics.
[07:05] Rajiv: We'll calculate cost using tokens generated and GPU seconds. We'll provide a spreadsheet with cost model assumptions.
[07:12] Priya: Also want quality metrics — for recommender we'll use relevance@10 and for convo search a recall/precision on a set of golden queries.
[07:19] Rajiv: We'll need your golden set and ranking labels.
[07:22] Priya: We'll prep a 200-query golden set with labels.
[07:26] Maya: Great. On instrumentation: do you need agents to inject traffic or can you accept a replay?
[07:32] Rajiv: Both. Replay is fine for reproducibility. For burst testing we'll do synthetic load with a distributed runner.
[07:40] Liam: Network egress — our security policy blocks outbound except to whitelisted IPs, will Redwood provide a static egress IP range for the test?
[07:48] Rajiv: For private peering there's no public egress; for hosted we can provide egress ranges but they may change. Since you're peering into your account, egress is internal and should pass.
[07:58] Marco: Ok good.
[08:00] Sofia: SOW specifics — acceptance criteria draft: p95 thresholds, precision@10 > baseline, audit logs streaming and retention 90 days, SAML login working with test IdP. Anything to add?
[08:12] Priya: Add security review sign-off from our security lead and documentation of KMS key IDs.
[08:17] Maya: We'll add that.
[08:20] Rajiv: One tradeoff note — if you want p95 under 300ms at 800 QPS bursts you'll need larger instance type or more replicas which affects cost. We'll show cost vs latency options.
[08:31] Liam: We'll review options but want to see cost implications.
[08:34] Maya: For the benchmark run we'll propose three configs: small (minimal), perf-optimized (low p95), and cost-optimized.
[08:43] Priya: Perfect.
[08:45] Marco: About logging retention — is 90 days max or will longer retention cost extra?
[08:50] Rajiv: We'll forward logs to your S3; retention policy is on your side. If you want Redwood to store logs longer we'll quote it as an add-on.
[08:59] Sofia: Ok, moving to timeline and scheduling specifics. We need the SOW and infra checklist to proceed.
[09:06] Maya: We'll ship SOW draft and infra checklist by 2026-05-07. Rajiv will share the benchmark runbook by 2026-05-11.
[09:14] Rajiv: For the runbook, we'll include exact payload sizes, concurrency profiles, seed prompts, and expected metrics.
[09:20] Priya: Also can you provide a sample of the audit log JSON schema?
[09:24] Rajiv: Yes, we'll include a sample.
[09:26] Maya: A couple of clarifying points from security — do you require any subprocessor approvals?
[09:32] Liam: We'll need a list of subprocessors and data flow map for legal.
[09:37] Maya: We'll attach the subprocessors list and dataflow diagram.
[09:40] Marco: What about penetration testing? We run internal pentests — will Redwood allow scoped pen tests against the pilot endpoints?
[09:47] Rajiv: We have a pentest policy — we can allow customer-led pentests if scoped and coordinated, usually after pilot kickoff and with a narrow window. We'll provide the authorization flow.
[09:57] Priya: Good.
[09:59] Sofia: Any blockers we should know now?
[10:02] Marco: For me the main blocker is networking — peering and firewall rules. We'll prioritize that.
[10:07] Liam: Security sign-off on SOC2 artifacts may take a few days.
[10:11] Maya: Understood. Quick note on data residency — do you require EU-only regions or is us-east fine?
[10:17] Priya: For this pilot US-only is fine, but production may need EU. We'll document that as a future requirement.
[10:24] Rajiv: We can schedule region-specific tests later.
[10:28] Maya: Anything else on the technical side?
[10:31] Priya: Will the pilot include canary fallback rules? If the primary model hits errors, do you expose a simpler variant?
[10:38] Rajiv: Yes Redwood supports automatic fallback routing to smaller model variants; we can configure that for the pilot and capture fallback rates.
[10:46] Liam: Ok we want to monitor fallback frequency.
[10:49] Rajiv: We'll track that metric.
[10:51] Maya: Recap of concrete outputs we'll send: SOC2/ISO artifacts, subprocessors, SAML and KMS integration guides, infra checklist, SOW draft, benchmark runbook, audit log sample.
[11:03] Priya: And from Sycamore: sanitized traffic traces, golden queries, test IdP, network peering info.
[11:10] Sofia: Let's lock the benchmark window — aiming week of May 18th. Do we need a 2-hour window or more?
[11:17] Rajiv: For baseline we'll schedule a 2-hour controlled run; additional runs are helpful but let's start with 2 hours.
[11:24] Marco: We'll reserve 4 hours in case we need retries.
[11:27] Maya: Great, I'll propose a calendar invite for May 19th 14:00-16:00 UTC as primary.
[11:34] Liam: Works for me.
[11:36] Priya: Works.
[11:38] Maya: Any last questions?
[11:40] Priya: One small one — how are model versions managed during pilot? We don't want silent updates.
[11:46] Rajiv: You can pin model version for the pilot; Redwood will not auto-upgrade without explicit rollout config. We'll show versioning controls.
[11:55] Liam: Good.
[11:57] Maya: OK that's it from our side. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts.
[12:02] Marco: Thanks, bye.
[12:04] End meeting.
